_note: Laboratory tests of the PG specification. Original drawings (SVG, 160 x 120) and descriptions written for this app; used by the page, the PDF and the Colab notebook.

tests.name: Flash Point
tests.purpose: Safety check. The binder is heated in an open cup while a small flame passes over it; the flash point is the temperature at which the vapours first ignite briefly.

tests.name: Rotational Viscometer
tests.purpose: A spindle turns in the hot binder and the torque gives its viscosity at 135 °C. It shows that the binder can be pumped and mixed, and gives mixing and compaction temperatures.

tests.name: Dynamic Shear Rheometer
tests.purpose: A thin binder disc between two plates is twisted back and forth. The complex modulus G* and phase angle δ describe stiffness and elasticity: G*/sin δ controls rutting, G*·sin δ controls fatigue cracking.

tests.name: Rolling Thin Film Oven
tests.purpose: Simulates ageing during mixing and laying: thin binder films in rotating glass bottles are exposed to hot air at 163 °C for 85 minutes. The residue is tested in the DSR and the mass change is checked.

tests.name: Pressure Aging Vessel
tests.device: Heated pressure vessel with pan rack
tests.purpose: Simulates several years of ageing in service: the RTFO residue in thin pans is held at high temperature under 2.10 MPa air pressure for 20 hours. The aged binder is then tested in the DSR, BBR and DTT.

tests.name: Bending Beam Rheometer
tests.device: Three-point bending in a cold bath
tests.purpose: A small binder beam rests on two supports in a cold liquid bath and a constant load pushes its middle down. The deflection gives the creep stiffness S and its rate of change m, which control thermal cracking.

tests.name: Direct Tension Tester
tests.device: Tension test of a dog-bone specimen
tests.purpose: A small dog-bone binder specimen is pulled apart at low temperature until it breaks. The failure strain shows whether the binder can stretch enough before cracking; it is used when the BBR stiffness is between 300 and 600 MPa.
